pull.title: wallet: rpc: Deprecate `encryptwallet` RPC for encrypting existing wallets.
pull.body:
For more context, see: #36027

Encrypting existing wallets that are unencrypted is fraught with footguns and complexity both for users and for developers.

For example:

- No efforts are made to ensure that remnants of unencrypted key material are not left on the user's disk, as attempting to ensure this would be difficult and dangerous, and for some SSD's infeasible.

- Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user. (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26607)

- Because new keys are made after encryption, restoring from a backup made before encryption may result in loss of funds.

_LLM Disclosure: Used gemma4-26B and qwen3.8-next-flash as research and drafting tools, but all code and text present here were written by me._

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.
Concept ACK, will review when I get a chance.

Concept ACK

I think `encryptwallet` RPC was created before the `createwalllet` gained the `passphrase`, and for what it worth creating today a new encrypted wallet and sendall-ing to it is equivalent and cleaner.

The GUI "Encrypt Wallet…" action (`WalletView::encryptWallet` → `interfaces::Wallet::encryptWallet`) is unaffected and is probably where most users hit this. It might be worth mentioning in the description and release notes so the GUI and RPC deprecations ship in the same release (?).

Left some nits.

refactor: test: Avoid encryptwallet in interface_bitcoin_cli.py

This RPC will be deprecated in a future commit, so tests should avoid
relying on it. This commit also adds scaffolding to init_wallet that
will be used when refactoring other tests.

refactor: test: rpc_psbt.py extract encrypted wallet signing

This improves legibility of the test and avoids the use of
`encryptwallet` which will be deprecated.
refactor: test: wallet_bumpfee.py isolate encrypted wallet tests

refactor: test: wallet_fundrawtransaction.py avoid encryptwallet

A later commit will deprecate this RPC.

refactor: test: wallet_listdescriptors.py extract encrypted wallet test

Co-authored-by: Pablo Martin <pablomartin4btc@gmail.com>
test: refactor: wallet_multiwallet.py use a new encrypted wallet

refactor: test: signrawtransaction isolate encrypted wallet test

This is useful since a future commit will deprecate `encryptwallet`.

wallet: rpc: Deprecate `encryptwallet`

Encrypting wallets from creation will still be supported, but there are
footguns both for users and for developers in supporting wallets that
are created unencrypted and then later become encrypted.

The functional tests where the `deprecatedrpc` argument is added are
ones where functionality or behavior of `encryptwallet` is being tested,
they should be kept until the RPC command is removed.

comments.body:
nit: the two branches only differ in the passphrase and the unlock around the import, so they could perhaps be collapsed. Also `w` is assigned but then `get_wallet_rpc` is called again for `wallet_importprivkey`, so `w` could be reused there.

Since this drops the `if wallet_name is not None:` check, the `wallet_names` [comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4303f3b7f0775cdbbe77faddf142e1e44fa590ca/test/functional/test_framework/test_framework.py#L121-L122) could also drop "If wallet names are None, wallet creation is skipped.". That case has been broken since #32452 (fcc457573f) anyway (`get_wallet_rpc(None)` would rase in `urllib.parse.quote`).

```suggestion
            passphrase_args = {"passphrase": self.default_wallet_pass} if encrypted else {}
            n.createwallet(wallet_name=wallet_name, load_on_startup=True, **passphrase_args)
            w = n.get_wallet_rpc(wallet_name)
            with WalletUnlock(w, self.default_wallet_pass) if encrypted else contextlib.nullcontext():
                wallet_importprivkey(w, n.get_deterministic_priv_key().key, 0, label="coinbase")                
```

(needs import contextlib; tested on top of 2cc0946985 with the full extended functional suite.)

In 2587fe96a8c54a97d2dd9c9d9fcc7d3ceda441b4 "refactor: test: rpc_psbt.py extract encrypted wallet signing"

This logging is unnecessary.

As we've discussed elsewhere, the main purpose of that convention/recommendation is to avoid naming collisions, but it has the downside that it also requires the PR to be opened before the release note can be made. I think it's a matter of preference which I feel a bit stubbornly about so I'll mark this as resolved.
